## Classification error metrics demo

Open the [classification error metrics demo](assets/threshold-explorer-standalone.html){target="_blank"} in a web browser.

Suppose you fit a logistic regression model on a large spam dataset similar to the one from the logistic regression lecture. For example, the model may have been fit to data from 1,000 emails.

This demo shows the results of applying the fitted logistic regression model above to 10 new emails. Answer the following questions. 

1. How many of the 10 emails are actually spam? How do you know?
2. Which email has the largest gap between its estimated probability of being spam and its actual spam classification? How big is the gap? Could this gap ever exceed 1 for an email outside of this dataset?
3. What is the demo's default threshold for converting estimated probabilities to predictions?
4. Under the default threshold, how many emails are predicted to be spam?
5. Under the default threshold, what is the accuracy of the model?
6. Under the default threshold, what fraction of spam emails were correctly classified? What metric does this question correspond to?
7. Under the default threshold, what fraction of real emails were correctly classified? What metric does this question correspond to?
8. Under the default threshold, what fraction of spam emails were classified as real? What metric does this correspond to?
9. Under the default threshold, what fraction of real emails were classified as spam? What metric does this correspond to?
10. Why is the denominator of all four error metrics constant? Is the denominator of these metrics constant in all binary classification scenarios, or is this specific to this situation?
11. What is the AUC of the model? What is the plain English interpretation of this model's AUC that could be fully understood by someone who had only taken Data 8 or Stat 20? Your answer should include the word "probability".
12. Slowly increase the threshold. Is the number of emails predicted to be spam increasing, decreasing, or staying flat? Why is this happening?
13. When you increase the threshold, the FPR cannot increase. Why?
14. When you decrease the threshold, is the total number of emails predicted to be real increasing, decreasing, or staying flat? Why?
15. When you increase the threshold, the FNR can never decrease. Why?
16. When you increase the threshold, you move down the ROC curve. Why?
17. What threshold corresponds to the top right of the ROC curve? Why?
18. Does the position on the ROC curve always change when you change the threshold? Why or why not?
19. When you change the threshold, the AUC does not change. Why?
20. Does accuracy always move in one direction when you move the threshold in one direction?
21. Go look at the definition of precision in the lecture slides. Write a real-world interpretation of precision in the context of the demo that could be understood by someone who has only taken Data 8 or Stat 20. Your definition cannot use the words positive or negative, or abbreviations of them.
22. Repeat the previous question, but for the negative predictive value metric from the slides.
